qwen38_27b.name: Qwen3.8 27B
qwen38_27b.description: Dense 27B model that can think or answer straight away.

main.name: Qwen3.8 27B (4-bit)
main.description: Good quality. 16-29 tok/s. About 20 GiB of memory.

quality.note: ESTIMATE for the quantised build run here: Artificial Analysis scores the full-precision hosted model, and no score has been published for this quant. Full precision scores 20 at the highest reasoning setting (18 at medium). 4-bit usually costs 0-1 point (range 19-20).

rankings.note: An aggregate index built mostly from vendor-reported benchmarks. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

Agentic coding, reported by the vendor. Best of two harnesses (Claude Code, mini-SWE-agent) at xhigh reasoning. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

Human preference votes, rank 85 in the 2026-11-22 snapshot (37,444 votes), read through LMArena's Hugging Face mirror because arena.ai blocks scripts. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.
The coding category of LiveBench 2.0, run by the LiveBench team (independent). Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

Reported by Qwen on its model card; no sample count or effort stated. Artificial Analysis measured 90.5 at its highest effort. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

Reported by Qwen on its model card (agent 'Terminus'). Terminal-Bench 2.1 has no official board and sources differ widely: Qwen3.8 27B scores 58.4 on Vals, 73.0 on its card and 79.8 on Artificial Analysis, so gaps between sources are as large as gaps between models. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

flash_next.name: Qwen3.8 Flash-Next
flash_next.description: Large mixture-of-experts model that stays fast for its size.

fast.name: Gyro-S
fast.description: Good quality. 80-110 tok/s. About 34 GiB of memory.

quality.note: ESTIMATE for the quantised build run here: Artificial Analysis scores the full-precision hosted model, and no score has been published for this quant. Full precision scores 28. Gyro-S (TQ1_0) has the largest measured drift from the original (KL divergence 0.33, top-1 agreement 77%, agentionai's card), so a loss of about 2-6 points is assumed (range 22-26).

quality.name: Gyro-M
quality.description: Better quality. 60-70 tok/s. About 38 GiB of memory.

quality.note: ESTIMATE for the quantised build run here: Artificial Analysis scores the full-precision hosted model, and no score has been published for this quant. Full precision scores 28. Gyro-M (TQ2_0) drifts less (KL divergence 0.29, top-1 agreement 79%), so a loss of about 1-3 points is assumed (range 25-27).

large.name: Gyro-L
large.description: Highest quality (matched M in our tests). 50-55 tok/s. About 38 GiB of memory.

quality.note: ESTIMATE for the quantised build run here: Artificial Analysis scores the full-precision hosted model, and no score has been published for this quant. Full precision scores 28. Gyro-L drifts least (KL divergence 0.15, top-1 agreement 84%), so a loss of under 1 point is assumed (range 27-28).

license.note: Free to use, including commercially. A separate licence is needed only to run a Model-as-a-Service or AI work-assistant business; large products (100M monthly users or US$20M monthly revenue) must credit the model.

rankings.note: An aggregate index built mostly from vendor-reported benchmarks. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

Agentic coding, reported by the vendor. Best of two harnesses (Claude Code, mini-SWE-agent) at xhigh reasoning. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

Reported by Qwen on its model card; no sample count or effort stated. Artificial Analysis measured 92.3. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

Artificial Analysis harness (Terminus 2, pass@1 over 3 runs), read through BenchLM and not checked on Artificial Analysis itself. Terminal-Bench 2.1 has no official board and sources differ widely: Qwen3.8 27B scores 58.4 on Vals, 73.0 on its card and 79.8 on Artificial Analysis, so gaps between sources are as large as gaps between models. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

hy4_flash.name: Tencent Hy4-Flash
hy4_flash.description: Large mixture-of-experts model from Tencent. Reads pictures.

main.name: SQ-64
main.description: Good quality. 15-18 tok/s. About 36 GiB of memory.

license.weights: Tencent Hy License 1.0 (Apache-2.0 with extra terms)
license.note: Apache-2.0 plus extra terms in section 10 for large Model-as-a-Service operators; ordinary internal use is not affected.

rankings.note: An aggregate index built mostly from vendor-reported benchmarks. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

Agentic coding, reported by the vendor. Second-hand: Tencent's figure (Thinking High, with tools) as quoted by a mirror, harness not stated. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

Indicative only: Tencent publishes no GPQA figure. This is OpenRouter's quality panel for providers serving Hy4-Flash (88.2 to 91.2 by provider), a different method from the model-card figures of the other local models. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

Vals AI, mini-swe-agent, average of 3 runs, snapshot 2026-11-19. Tencent's card says 19.2 and tbench.ai's 4.1 board 11.8. Scores the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here, so the build may score lower.

inkling2.name: Inkling 2 Mini
inkling2.description: Always thinks before it answers; lower effort levels shorten that on small jobs.

main.name: Inkling 2 Mini (oQ 4-bit)
main.description: Good quality. 60-90 tok/s. About 24 GiB of memory.

quality.note: ESTIMATE for the quantised build run here: Artificial Analysis scores the full-precision hosted model, and no score has been published for this quant. Full precision scores 20 (20.1 on the vendor's card). The vendor's own checkpoint is already mixed NVFP4 and MXFP8, and this oQ4e build (about 4.9 bits per weight) keeps attention at 8 bits, so little loss is assumed.

meeting_notes.name: Meeting notes
meeting_notes.description: A recording or transcript in; a transcript with speakers, a summary, action items and decisions out.

mac.name: This Mac (MLX)
mac.description: Speech recognition and speaker detection run on this Mac, about 4 minutes per hour of recording.

license.weights: Qwen3-ASR: Apache-2.0. Speaker detection: pyannote segmentation 3.0 (MIT) and NVIDIA TitaNet-S (Apache-2.0, the NeMo toolkit licence).
license.code: sherpa-onnx and RapidOCR with its PaddleOCR models: Apache-2.0. mlx-audio and mlx-lm: MIT. ffmpeg runs as a separate program.
license.note: Every speech, speaker and name-reading piece is permissively licensed. The notes themselves come from the text model you pick, which has its own licence; check it on its card.

qwen_image.name: Qwen Image 2.1
qwen_image.description: Pictures from a written description, with legible lettering. Turbo is fast; the full model is slower and finer.

mlx.name: Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo (MLX, 8-bit)
mlx.description: 8 steps, one picture every 15-25 s. Each picture runs in its own process (--low-ram), so memory is held only while one is being made.

quality.note: Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, 5,535 votes. Rated on the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here.

qwen21.name: Qwen Image 2.1 (MLX, 8-bit, best quality)
qwen21.description: The full model behind Turbo: 30 guided steps with a negative prompt, about 100 s per 1024x1024 picture and 16 GiB while it runs.

quality.note: Qwen-Image-2.1, 6,551 votes. Rated on the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here.

license.note: Research and evaluation only; any commercial use needs a separate licence from Qwen. Use Qwen-Image 2512 or Z-Image Turbo for work.

yue2.name: YuE2 songs
yue2.description: Full songs with vocals from lyrics and a style description (the MLX port; non-commercial licence).

mlx.name: YuE2 3B (MLX, 8-bit)
mlx.description: About real time: a three-minute song takes about three minutes. Language model in 8 bits, audio model in bf16.

quality.note: Scored by the YuE2 authors on their WildSongBench, so it is vendor-run. Automatic metric (a model judges the song), not listener votes. Best-of-8 sampling scores 6.96.

mlx.name: Qwen3-TTS 1.7B (MLX, 8-bit)
mlx.description: Qwen's Qwen3-TTS 12Hz 1.7B in 8 bits: CustomVoice, VoiceDesign and Base, one in memory at a time. Apache 2.0.

quality.note: ESTIMATE: Artificial Analysis rates a model called Qwen3 TTS (3,230 votes) without saying which checkpoint; the open 1.7B weights run here have no score of their own.

mlx.name: OmniVoice (MLX, bf16)
mlx.description: OmniVoice in 646+ languages, voice cloning or a described voice. The model is CC BY-NC: non-commercial use only.

license.weights: CC BY-NC (non-commercial); its audio tokenizer adds a 100,000-user cap

mlx.name: Drama 3 (MLX, 3-bit)
mlx.description: Fish Audio's Drama 3 with speaker tags and scenes, 3-bit. Fish Audio Community License: free below USD 500,000 annual revenue, no hosted services.

license.note: Free only while the annual revenue of you and your affiliates is under US$500,000, so not for company use here; no hosted service for third parties either. Output may not train other speech models.

quality.note: Fish Audio Drama 3, 2,145 votes, rank 9 of 106. Rated on the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here.

mlx.name: S2 Pro (MLX, 8-bit)
mlx.description: Fish Audio S2 Pro with [cue] tags. Fish Audio Research License: research and personal use only.

license.note: Research and personal use only. The licence counts a company's internal operations as commercial use.

quality.note: Fish Audio S2 Pro, 3,154 votes, rank 48. Its newer S2.1 Pro scores 1182. Rated on the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here.

mlx.name: Breeze TTS 2 (MLX, 8-bit)
mlx.description: English and Chinese speech from a described or cloned voice. BreezeBlue non-commercial licence.

license.note: Non-commercial use only, including no use for an organisation's internal operations.

quality.note: Breeze TTS 2, 3,249 votes, rank 15. One score for English and Chinese. Rated on the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here.

wan_video.name: Wan 2.2 video
wan_video.description: Short clips from a description or a first picture (Apache-2.0).

mlx.name: Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B (MLX, 8-bit)
mlx.description: 832x480, up to 1.4 s, about 100 s per clip. The model is loaded for each clip, and the clip needs about 29 GiB while it runs.

quality.note: ESTIMATE: Arena AI rates Wan 2.2 A14B (1131.78), not the 5B run here, so this is an upper bound. Read through the benchmarklist.com mirror of arena.ai (dated 2026-11-10).

qwen_image_2512.name: Qwen-Image 2512
qwen_image_2512.description: Qwen's December 2025 base model (Apache-2.0): 20 guided steps with a negative prompt. Heavy: about 37 GiB while a picture is made.

qwen2512.name: Qwen-Image 2512 (MLX, 8-bit; heavy)
qwen2512.description: Qwen's December 2025 base model, Apache-2.0: 20 steps with a negative prompt. Needs about 37 GiB while a picture is made and takes 4-5 minutes, so only start it with the other models stopped.

quality.note: ESTIMATE: Artificial Analysis does not rate 2512. Z-Image Turbo's 937 plus the 42 points Arena AI puts 2512 above it (1124 vs 1082). Low confidence, two arenas combined.

z_image.name: Z-Image Turbo
z_image.description: Tongyi-MAI's 6B distilled picture model (Apache-2.0): 9 steps, about 20 s per picture.

zimage.name: Z-Image Turbo (MLX, 8-bit)
zimage.description: Tongyi-MAI's 6B distilled model, Apache-2.0. 9 steps, one picture in about 16-20 s; no negative prompt.

quality.note: Z-Image Turbo, 9,034 votes. Rated on the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here.

h3_video.name: MiniMax H3 video
h3_video.description: Short clips with sound from a description or from first and last pictures, through the h3.c Metal engine. Personal use only: the H3 licence excludes the US, EU, UK and South Korea.

mlx.name: MiniMax H3 (Metal, SSD streaming)
mlx.description: The original BF16 weights streamed from the SSD: about 11 GiB while a clip is made. A 5 s clip at 480p takes about 3 minutes as a draft.

license.weights: MiniMax H3 Community License (excludes the US, EU, UK and South Korea)
license.note: Rights are granted only outside the US, EU, UK and South Korea, and use there is not licensed. Keep it to your own machine.

quality.note: MiniMax H3, 29,257 votes. Read through the benchmarklist.com mirror of arena.ai (dated 2026-11-10). Rated on the hosted full-precision model, not the quantised build run here.

rankings.note: MiniMax H3 on the open-weights board. Blind human votes run by Artificial Analysis; rated on the hosted model, not the quantised build run here.

ace_step.name: ACE-Step songs
ace_step.description: Songs with vocals, or instrumentals, from a style and lyrics (MIT). Fast: 30 s of music in about 10 s.

mlx.name: ACE-Step 1.5 turbo (MLX)
mlx.description: 8 diffusion steps with the 1.7B planning model. About 14 GiB resident; two-minute songs peak near 21 GiB.

license.note: MIT code and weights, no territory or revenue clause found; the card says the music may be used commercially. The training-data claim (licensed, royalty-free and synthetic data) is the vendor's own and unverified, so legal review of the data is still advisable.

quality.note: Scored by the YuE2 authors on WildSongBench, not by ACE-Step's makers. Phoneme error 7.5%. The Artificial Analysis arena leader 'ACE Music v1' is not documented as this model.

minimax_music.name: MiniMax Music 3
minimax_music.description: Songs with vocals, or instrumentals, from a style and lyrics. Check its licence terms before company use.

mlx.name: MiniMax Music 3 (MLX, 8-bit)
mlx.description: The mxfp8 build, 13 GB. About 14 GiB resident for a 30 s song.

license.weights: MiniMax-Music3 Community License (MIT-style with commercial terms)
license.note: Free to use. Treated as work use because the app is an internal tool, not a product or service offered to others (the owner's reading, not legal advice). If it becomes one, the licence requires "MiniMax-Music3" displayed on the interface, MiniMax's written authorisation above US$20 million yearly revenue from such products or services, safeguards against misuse when offered to third parties, and indemnifying MiniMax for breaches. No territory exclusion.

quality.note: Scored by the YuE2 authors on WildSongBench, not by MiniMax. Best lyric accuracy of the three (phoneme error 6.3% against 7.5% ACE-Step and 8.4% YuE2). MiniMax rewrites the style prompt before generating.

ltx_video.name: LTX-2.5 video
ltx_video.description: Short clips with sound from a description or a first picture. Personal use only: a company above US$10M revenue needs a paid licence.

mlx.name: LTX-2.5 distilled (MLX, 4-bit)
mlx.description: Up to 1280x704 and 5 s with sound. About half a minute for a 4 s quick clip, 2.5 minutes sharp. Needs about 14 GiB while it runs.

license.weights: LTX-2.x Community License (paid licence needed above US$10M annual revenue)
license.note: Section 2.1: entities with annual revenues of at least US$10,000,000 (affiliates included) need a paid licence for any use except non-commercial purposes. Section 2.2 limits those to personal hobby use unconnected to any employer, or a company's testing, evaluation and R&D in a non-production environment. So it is personal here; at work only for evaluation.

quality.note: Artificial Analysis rates the hosted LTX-2.5 Fast (938) and Pro (932); this is the 4-bit distilled build, which should be close to Fast but is not rated itself. Blind human votes run by Artificial Analysis.

fastmetal_video.name: FastMetal video
fastmetal_video.description: Short clips from a description, fast: distilled Wan models, 3 denoise steps (Apache-2.0). No first picture and no sound.

5b.name: FastMetal 5B (1280x704)
5b.description: Wan 2.2 5B distilled. Up to 5 s at 1280x704; a 3 s clip takes about a minute (35 s in faster mode). Needs about 26 GiB while a new description is encoded, 12 GiB after.

14b.name: FastMetal 14B (832x480)
14b.description: Wan 2.1 14B distilled. Up to 5 s at 832x480; a 3 s clip takes about 2.5 minutes (67 s in faster mode). About 22 GiB while it runs.

license.code: FastVideo: Apache-2.0 (TAEHV and RIFE decoders: MIT)
license.note: Distilled from Wan 2.2 TI2V 5B and Wan 2.1 T2V 14B, both Apache-2.0. The first run downloads a small TAEHV decoder file from GitHub once.

longcat_video.name: LongCat video
longcat_video.description: Short clips from a description, without sound (MIT). Slow: under a minute for the shortest clip.

q8.name: LongCat-Video 13.6B (MLX, 8-bit)
q8.description: 832x480 at 15 fps, 0.6 to 4 seconds, from a description. About 45 seconds for the shortest clip, 6 minutes for four seconds. Needs 19 to 37 GiB while a clip is made.

license.code: longcat-video-mlx: MIT (declared in its pyproject.toml and README; the repository has no LICENSE file)
license.note: Meituan's LongCat-Video is MIT. The MLX port needs two fixes that the worker's driver applies without editing it: merging the fast LoRA into the quantised weights, and giving the first-frame latents timestep 0.

decide_karpo.name: Karpo 31B
decide_karpo.description: Answers a question about a situation with a probability for each answer. Text only; the most accurate of the three here.

mxfp4.name: Karpo 31B (MLX, mxfp4)
mxfp4.description: About 0.25 s for a short situation, 3 s for 2,000 tokens. Needs about 20 GiB while it runs.

license.code: Apache-2.0 (MLX port by audreyt, derived from Gemma 4, also Apache-2.0)
license.note: The weights and inference code are Apache-2.0; attribution is requested but not required. This is a community MLX port of the official model, text only (the picture tower is removed).

decide_pplx.name: pplx-decider 27B
decide_pplx.description: Answers a question about a situation, with pictures, with a probability for each answer. Perplexity's decision model on Qwen3.8 27B.

q8.name: pplx-decider v1.2 (MLX, 8-bit)
q8.description: About 0.5 s for a short situation, 3.7 s for 3,000 words. Reads pictures. Needs about 30 GiB while it runs.

license.note: Derived from Qwen3.8 27B (Apache-2.0). No use restrictions on the card.

quality.note: pplx-decider v1.2 on JevBench at full precision; this is the 8-bit build.

pplx-decider v1.2 on the Artificial Analysis decision index (as shown by benchlm.ai); this is the 8-bit build.

decide_h2o.name: H2O-Lightning 4B
decide_h2o.description: A small, fast decision model that also reads pictures, with a probability for each answer.

bf16.name: H2O-Lightning 4B (MLX, bf16)
bf16.description: About 0.15 s for a short situation, 1 s for 3,000 words. Reads pictures. Needs about 12 GiB while it runs.

license.note: The 4B is Apache-2.0. H2O-Lightning 31B is a different licence (non-commercial), so do not swap it in.

quality.note: H2O-Lightning 4B on JevBench, run at full precision as here.

decide_torchcast.name: Torchcast 4B
decide_torchcast.description: Answers a question about a situation with a probability for each answer. Text only; small and fast.

bf16.name: Torchcast 4B v1.3 (bf16, Mac GPU)
bf16.description: About 0.15 s for a short situation, 1.5 s for 6,000 tokens. Needs about 14 GiB while it runs.

license.weights: Apache-2.0 (v1.3.1 and later; v1.1 was CC BY-NC)
license.note: Based on Qwen3.5-4B (Apache-2.0). Use the v1.3.1 release: earlier releases keep a non-commercial licence. The 12B and 27B Torchcast models are CC BY-NC, so personal use only.
